OSINT analysis of registered federal lobbying activities, institutional influence mapping, and the translation of lobbying communications into policy outcomes. All data sourced from the Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying of Canada.

LIRIL's OSINT analysis scanned the Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying registry and identified 8 core CIJA lobbying nodes connected to 42 institutional and political entities . The underlying data is drawn from the public lobbying registry.

The Lobbying Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. 44) requires organizations that communicate with federal public office holders to register and report their activities. The Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying maintains a public registry of all registered lobbying communications. Each entry records: the registrant, the subject matter, the government institution contacted, the designated public office…

On January 19, 2026 , the Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying implemented a significant change to the lobbying registration threshold. Organizations now trigger mandatory registration when any employee spends 8 or more hours on lobbying communications within a consecutive four-week period — replacing the previous “significant part of duties” standard (approximately 20% threshold ). Source: Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying — open.canada.ca proactive disclosure, synced 2026-04-13.

Separately, the Conflict of Interest Act requires MPs and ministers to disclose sponsored travel paid for by outside organizations. These disclosures are published by the Office of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner.

Extensive lobbying on online hate speech legislation. Communications to Justice, Heritage, and Public Safety. The bill's definition of "hate speech" and enforcement mechanisms were key lobbying targets. 45+ communications on this subject from multiple registered organizations.

Lobbying for government adoption of the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition of antisemitism. Communications to PMO, Heritage, and Justice. Canada formally adopted the definition in 2019 following sustained lobbying engagement.
